Testimony of the Maine Municipal Association (MMA) Neither For Nor Against
LD 807, An Act to Limit the Number of Free Motor Vehicle Registrations |That May be Provided to a Disables Veteran and Reimburse Municipalities for the Loss of Excise Tax
April 3, 2025 ________________________________________________________________
Senator Nangle, Representative Crafts and distinguished members of the Joint Standing Committee on Transportation, my name is Amanda Campbell, and I am submitting testimony on behalf of the Maine Municipal Association's 70-member Legislative Policy Committee (LPC) neither for nor against LD 807.
Municipal officials overwhelmingly appreciate the service and sacrifices made by our nation's veterans and their families.
LD 807 looks to limit the number of free motor vehicle registrations that an eligible veteran may obtain to three. Current statute provides no limitation which has caused, in some member communities, significant loss of excise tax creating a shift in burden to the rest of the community, including the veteran receiving the excise tax exemption. With few guardrails in place on the program, some municipalities have seen multiple vehicles, registered at no cost, to veterans and members of their families. One community alone reported 26 vehicles registered to nine veterans, since July 1, 2024, with an excise tax loss of nearly $8,600. These figures include seven registrations to one single registrant.
This procedure is simply unsustainable, especially in an atmosphere of increased costs for municipal services and increased property taxes. Excise taxes are retained by the municipality and are used directly towards reducing the overall tax burden of a community. When those revenues are lost through an exemption, everyone pays the difference.
The bill today would amend 29-A MRSA �523, sub-�2 by limiting the number of free registrations to three and adding language that would require municipalities to submit a report to the SOS office outlining the number of free registrations and the amount of excise tax lost. After receiving a subsequent report from the SOS office, the State Controller would reimburse municipalities for the lost excise tax revenue.

Although this language provides for reimbursement of lost excise tax revenue, the reporting requirements, which require data not already accessible through municipal registration software, could trigger the state mandate reimbursement requirement under the Maine Constitution, Article IX, Section 21, for 90% of municipal administrative costs. It is also likely that updates to registration software, at both the state and local level, would be required.
Last fall, in conversations between MMA and the Secretary of State's office, language for a potential solution to this concern was discussed that would instead amend 36 MRSA �1483, by requiring that disabled veterans who are eligible for the free registration outlined in Title 29-A, would be limited in number of registrations that are also eligible for an excise tax exemption. The vehicles would also be required to be "titled in the name of the veteran," a guardrail that would guarantee it is the veteran registrant receiving the benefit.
Municipal officials appreciate the intent of this bill, and I look forward to working with the sponsor, the committee and the SOS office on a solution that meets the needs of both veterans and the municipalities.
Thank you for the opportunity to speak with you and share the municipal perspective on this important topic. Please feel free to contact me or any member of the MMA Advocacy team with any questions related to municipal operations.

TESTIMONY OF MICHAEL J. ALLEN, ASSOCIATE COMMISSIONER FOR TAX POLICY
DEPARTMENT OF ADMINISTRATIVE AND FINANCIAL SERVICES
Before the Joint Standing Committee on Transportation Hearing Date: April 3, 2025
LD 807 - "An Act to Limit the Number of Free Motor Vehicle Registrations That May Be Provided to a Disabled Veteran and Reimburse Municipalities for the Loss
of Excise Taxes"
Senator Nagle, Representative Crafts, and members of the Transportation Committee - good afternoon, my name is Michael Allen, Associate Commissioner for Tax Policy in the Department of Administrative and Financial Services. I am testifying at the request of the Administration Neither For Nor Against LD 807, "An Act to Limit the Number of Free Motor Vehicle Registrations That May Be Provided to a Disabled Veteran and Reimburse Municipalities for the Loss of Excise Taxes."
First, the bill does not outline the timeline by which municipalities must notify the Secretary of State of lost revenues, or the process by which the State Controller must distribute those revenues to municipalities. Furthermore, the bill requires that the Secretary of State determine the amount of excise tax lost revenue and notify the State Controller of the amount of revenue to be reimbursed to each municipality. However, the bill does not specify whether these amounts are the same. These aspects of the program should be clarified.
Second, the bill summary states that the bill is intended to limit the number of vehicles a disabled veteran may claim as exempt from excise tax. However, what the bill actually does is limit the number of free registrations a veteran is entitled to under Title 29-A. While veterans who receive free registration are
1

exempt from excise tax under 36 M.R.S. � 1483(12), that subsection also exempts from the excise tax other disabled veterans who are not required to have obtained free registration and would thus not be subject to the new limit in this bill.
Finally, this bill creates the first reimbursement program for revenues lost because of excise tax exemptions - the potential precedent set by the bill should be carefully considered.
A fiscal estimate of the costs associated with this bill is not available at this time, but the creation of a new reimbursement program would incur a fiscal cost. The Secretary of State would have the best data to estimate the amount of state reimbursement. The administrative costs are also unclear at this time, but some costs would likely be incurred by the Secretary of State to administer the reimbursements.
The Administration looks forward to working with the Committee on the bill; representatives from MRS will be here for the Work Session to provide additional information and respond in detail to the Committee's questions.

JOINT STANDING COMMITTEE ON TRANSPORTATION
L.D. 807 "An Act to Limit the Number of Free Motor Vehicle Registration that May Be Provided
to a Disabled Veteran and Reimburse Municipalities for the Loss of Excise Taxes."
Testimony of Shenna Bellows, Secretary of State and Cathie Curtis, Deputy Secretary for the Bureau of Motor Vehicles,
Department of the Secretary of State
April 3, 2025
Senator Nangle, Representative Crafts, and Members of the Joint Standing Committee on Transportation,
I am providing testimony neither for nor against L.D. 807 "An Act to Limit the Nmnber of Free Motor Vehicle Registration that May Be Provided to a Disabled Veteran and Reimburse Municipalities for the
Loss of Excise Taxes."
This bill specifics that only 3 registered motor vehicles may be exempt from excise taxes for a disabled
veteran. lt also requires the State Controller to fiilly reimburse municipalities for the excise tax revenue lost from this exemption based on a report from the Secretary of State.
The Secretary of State's Office does not have any opinion regarding the limitation on the number of
vehicles that a disabled veteran may be exempted from excise tax.
However, we do see a couple of issues with this bill as written, related to the reimbursement of excise tax
revenue to the municipalities.
First, excise tax is a municipal tax and is retained by the municipality. Payment of excise tax is simply a prerequisite to a motor vehicle registration. The Secretary of State's office does not have authority over excise tax nor does excise tax from Maine residents go to the Highway fund. Therefore, the Secretary of State's Office respectfully asks to not be put in the middle of this excise tax matter. Municipalities should provide a report directly to another more appropriate state agency for excise tax reimbursement.
Second, this bill doesn't indicate from what account any lost excise tax revenue is reimbursed. We
believe the lost revenue should not be paid out of the Highway Fund.
I would like to suggest that prior to the work session, we work with the Representative Drinkwater and Maine Municipal Association to draft an amendment that would solve this problem from a different
approach and bring it back with to you.
Thank you for your time today and I will be happy to answer any questions.
